submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole peaks on the definite article 'the' and on possessive determiners (my, your, his, her, our, their, its) exactly when they open a noun phrase governed by the preposition 'on' (strongest, 1.5-2.5) or by a locative 'upon', 'onto', 'at' or 'by' (about 0.9-1.5), e.g. on the table, on my desk, at the station, by the river, upon the mat; the determiner of that prepositional complement is the peak token, while an indefinite article or a demonstrative in the same slot (on a mat, on this shelf, at a station) stays below the active line. It stays below the active line on 'the' after 'of', after 'in', 'with' and the relative-position prepositions (under, over, behind, beside, between, against, through, around, into, during, after, before), after an agentive 'by' in a passive (by the committee, by the government), when 'on' is selected by a stative verb of dependence, focus or commentary (depends on, relies on, focuses on, based on, comments on, reflects on), and on any determiner that is not a prepositional object (sentence-initial 'The', subject, direct object, or conjoined NP).
